description: Fixed review cameras for the placeholder room. World metres, +Y up, -Z forward (north). Positions do not follow the avatars, so captures stay comparable while the avatar profile changes. The first five are the Run 1 baseline; the fix round of 7 October reframed the companion camera for the 10 cm body (the other four are unchanged) and moved the review clock to 17:00 on 15 April, when the low sun comes through the west window onto both avatars. diorama_high and iso_room were added for the founder's 6 October art direction (high-angle and isometric views with a tilt-shift miniature feel); window_view and observe_view for his 7 October direction (the window's golden light and creamy bokeh; the observe view's very tight tilt-shift band). Focus points sit on the player's spawn or on the two avatars, whose reach and figures must stay crisp.

clock.note: Review captures pin the hour and date so time of day and season do not drift between rounds. 17:00 on 15 April (standard time, 30 degrees north): the sun stands 18 degrees up in the west, low enough to be golden and high enough to come through the west window (its sill is 0.5 m up) onto both avatars at the spawns, which the earlier 16:30 on 6 October (sun 14 degrees up, 256 degrees) never did. Spring, so the vibrant palette is what the frames show. Rounds before the fix round of 7 October used 16:30 on 6 October.

cameras.label: Player eye
cameras.purpose: What the 10 cm player sees: rug, book and doorstop within reach, the table and far wall beyond. Judges near crispness, far softening and how the floor reads at eye level.

cameras.label: Over the shoulder
cameras.purpose: The default play camera: just behind and above the player's left shoulder, the companion beside it. Judges the avatar against the room, its contact shadow, and the diorama depth of field.

cameras.label: Companion
cameras.purpose: In front of the two 10 cm avatars, at their head height, a little to their right and 0.4 to 0.7 m away, looking back at them across the book (a near blur in the corner) (they face north; the camera looks south). Judges both characters in one frame, their contact shadows, the west window's sun on them and the rug and doorstop up close. Reframed in the 7 October fix round: the old camera was placed for a 0.24 m companion and showed two specks.

cameras.label: Low corner
cameras.purpose: Floor level in the north-east corner looking across the room past the box: long floor perspective, contre-jour light, wall bases and corners.

cameras.label: Ceiling corner
cameras.purpose: High in the south-west corner looking down at the whole room: the tabletop-miniature view. Judges palette, warm key against cool shadow, the tilt-shift band and clutter density.

cameras.label: High-angle diorama
cameras.purpose: Run 1 art direction (6 October): a high-angle tilt-shift view framed on the two avatars from in front and to their left, about 1.4 m away at 45 degrees down with a 40-degree lens, so the rug, book and doorstop around them are in frame. Judges the tabletop-miniature read: the avatars and the rug around them crisp, the floor near the bottom of the frame and the far room at the top melting away, and the palette of the hour.

cameras.label: Isometric room
cameras.purpose: Run 1 art direction (6 October): an isometric-style overview from high by the north wall, about 35 degrees down (the isometric angle) with a narrow 30-degree lens, in front of the avatars (they face north) and a little to their right, looking across the room behind them to the south wall. Judges whether the whole room reads as an artistic handmade diorama rather than a photograph, with focus on the avatars and the rest of the room softening.

cameras.label: Window view
cameras.purpose: 7 October direction (golden window light, creamy bokeh) and review M2: from the floor by the east wall looking up at the west window with the two avatars crisp in the foreground. The pane must show the sky of the hour (it was a dark slate), the window must glow and light the room gold, and the bright window and lamp must melt into creamy bokeh behind the figures.

cameras.label: Observe view
cameras.purpose: 7 October direction: the observe profile, a very tight tilt-shift band for looking at what was built with the companion (Titl Shift 3.png). From the north looking south, square to the line between the two avatars so both stand at the same depth, the look's observe switch on: a sliver of the rug with both avatars crisp, everything nearer and farther melting away.

cameras.label: Observe view, F3 rig
cameras.purpose: Run 2, brief 07: what the founder saw in the third playtest. The real HUD's F3 view (the orbit camera 1.4 m out at 45 degrees, a 40-degree lens, the pivot on the player, shared with the companion while it is near) with the observe switch (O) on, and the focus the look gives that camera. The player must stand clearly in focus, whole.

cameras.label: Observe view, F4 rig
cameras.purpose: Run 2, brief 07: the same for the HUD's F4 view (2.7 m out at 35.26 degrees, a 30-degree lens), observe switch on.

sweep.note: The -Sweep contact sheet: one camera, rows winter, spring, summer and autumn (mid-season days), columns through the day on the solar model at 30 degrees north (standard time). The sun comes in through the west window only in the afternoon; 18:00 shows the seasonal swing at one clock time: night in winter and autumn, low sun in spring and summer.

light_checks.note: Pixel checks of light from real sources: at the review clock, floor points the physics says see the sun must brighten with it and points behind the walls must not; at 02:00 on the review date each night camera is saved with the lamps off and on. Contact crops of the avatars' feet judge whether 10 cm bodies look grounded under each source: the window's sky fill at the review clock, the low sun across the spawns on a summer evening (summer_sun) and the lamp at night (lamp_night).
